<!-- Generated by tools/docgen from doc comments. Do not edit: run scripts/docs.sh. -->

```odin
import dsp "fire:dsp"
```

DSP building blocks and ready-made nodes.

Every effect comes twice: as plain structs and procedures you can use inside
your own nodes (`svf_design` and `svf_tick`, `biquad_design`, ...), and as
a graph node with stable parameter ids (`filter_create`, `eq_create`, ...).
Primitives marked [rt] are safe on the audio thread.

```odin
// Inside your own node: one coefficient set, a state per channel.
c := dsp.svf_design(mode = .Lowpass, cutoff_hz = 800, q = 0.707, gain_db = 0, sample_rate = 48_000)
for &x in channel do x = f32(dsp.svf_tick(&c, &state[ch], f64(x)))

// As a node in a graph:
eq, _ := graph.add_node(g, dsp.eq_create(4), 2, 2)
graph.set_param(g, eq, dsp.eq_band_param(1, .Gain_Db), -6)
```

Also here: `Smoothed_Value` (parameter smoothing and automation ramps),
`Resampler`, the FFT and STFT, and the `Gain` and `One_Pole_Lowpass` nodes.
See /guides/effects/.

### Compressor

```odin
Compressor :: struct {
	threshold_db: f64,
	ratio: f64,
	knee_db: f64,
	attack_ms: f64,
	release_ms: f64,
	makeup: Smoothed_Value,
	mix: Smoothed_Value,
	detector: Level_Detector,
	gain: Gain_Smoother,
	sample_rate: f64,
	meter: u64,
}
```

A feed-forward compressor node, stereo-linked: one gain for all
channels, from the loudest. Input channels beyond the outputs are the
sidechain (add it with 4 inputs and 2 outputs for a stereo sidechain):
when there are any, they are detected instead of the main inputs.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `threshold_db` |  |
| `ratio` |  |
| `knee_db` |  |
| `attack_ms` |  |
| `release_ms` |  |
| `makeup` | dB |
| `mix` | percent |
| `detector` |  |
| `gain` |  |
| `sample_rate` |  |
| `meter` | atomic: f64 bits of the gain reduction in dB at the end of the last block |

### Convolver

```odin
Convolver :: struct {...}
```

Zero-latency convolution with one impulse response, for one channel.
The first `CONVOLVER_HEAD` taps are a direct FIR; taps up to
`CONVOLVER_SPLIT` use 64-frame FFT partitions; the rest use 1024-frame
partitions whose work is spread over the 1024 frames after each block
arrives, so a long response costs the same every frame instead of in
spikes (uniformly partitioned overlap-save at two sizes, after
Gardner, "Efficient Convolution without Input-Output Delay", JAES 1995).
Set up with `convolver_init`. Fields are internal.

### Convolution

```odin
Convolution :: struct {
	ir: [][]f32,
	convolvers: []Convolver,
	wet: []f32,
	mix: Smoothed_Value,
	wet_db: Smoothed_Value,
	allocator: mem.Allocator,
}
```

A convolution node (reverb from a recorded space, cabinet and speaker
simulation, any long FIR) with no latency. Its impulse response has one
channel for every output, or one per output channel. The response is
used as given: at the graph's sample rate (convert it with `Resampler`).

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `ir` | copied at create |
| `convolvers` |  |
| `wet` | a block of one channel's convolution |
| `mix` |  |
| `wet_db` |  |
| `allocator` |  |

### Delay

```odin
Delay :: struct {
	time_ms: f64,
	beats: f64,
	sync: bool,
	ping_pong: bool,
	primed: bool,
	low_cut: f64,
	high_cut: f64,
	frames: Smoothed_Value,
	feedback: Smoothed_Value,
	mix: Smoothed_Value,
	lines: []Delay_Line,
	low: Svf_Coeffs,
	high: Svf_Coeffs,
	low_state: []Svf_State,
	high_state: []Svf_State,
	sample_rate: f64,
}
```

An echo node: a delay with feedback, filtered in the loop, free or synced
to the tempo (`ctx.transport`; 120 BPM without one). Changing the time
glides there over about 100 ms, bending the echoes' pitch as tape does,
instead of clicking. Ping-pong takes the mix of the inputs and bounces
it between the first two outputs.

| `beats` |  |
| `sync` |  |
| `ping_pong` |  |
| `primed` | has rendered: before that, time changes jump instead of gliding |
| `low_cut` |  |
| `high_cut` |  |
| `frames` | the delay in frames, gliding |
| `feedback` |  |
| `mix` | percent |
| `lines` |  |
| `low` |  |
| `high` |  |
| `low_state` |  |
| `high_state` |  |
| `sample_rate` |  |

### Interpolation

```odin
Interpolation :: enum u8 {
	None,
	Linear,
	Cubic,
}
```

How a `Delay_Line` reads between samples.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `None` | the nearest older sample |
| `Linear` | cheap; dulls highs a little at fractional delays |
| `Cubic` | 4-point Hermite: smooth, for modulated delays (chorus, flanger) |

### Fft

```odin
Fft :: struct {...}
```

A complex FFT of a fixed size whose only prime factors are 2, 3 and 5
(see `fft_fast_size_above`). Unnormalised both ways: the forward
transform uses e^(−2πi·kn/N), the inverse e^(+2πi·kn/N), and an inverse
after a forward multiplies by N. f32 data, twiddles computed in f64.

A transform can run in one call or in `fft_steps` pieces (one per radix
stage), to spread its cost over several audio blocks. Set up with
`fft_init`; free with `fft_destroy`. One transform at a time per Fft.
Fields are internal.

### Real_Fft

```odin
Real_Fft :: struct {
	size: int,
	half_bin: bool,
	split: bool,
	complex: Fft,
	twiddles: []complex64,
	twists: []complex64,
	time: []complex64,
	freq: []complex64,
}
```

An FFT of `size` real samples (even; size/2 a fast size), giving size/2
complex bins. Same conventions as `Fft` (unnormalised; inverse after
forward multiplies by `size`). Two spectrum layouts:

- Normal: bin k is X[k] for 1 ≤ k < size/2, and bin 0 packs DC (real
  part) with Nyquist (imaginary part).
- Half-bin (`half_bin`): bin k is the spectrum at k + ½, for 0 ≤ k <
  size/2: X[k+½] = Σ x[n]·e^(−2πi·(k+½)n/size). No packing; the bins sit
  symmetrically around the frequencies that matter (used by STFTs).

With `split`, the final (forward) or first (inverse) twiddle pass is done
in two halves, for one more step and smaller pieces. Laid out as
Signalsmith Linear's RealFFT, so ported code steps through it the same
way. Set up with `real_fft_init`; free with `real_fft_destroy`. Fields are
internal.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `size` |  |
| `half_bin` |  |
| `split` |  |
| `complex` |  |
| `twiddles` |  |
| `twists` | half-bin: e^(−2πi·n/size), applied to the input pairs |
| `time` |  |
| `freq` |  |

```odin
Filter :: struct {
	mode: Filter_Mode,
	cutoff: Smoothed_Value,
	q: Smoothed_Value,
	gain_db: Smoothed_Value,
	coeffs: Svf_Coeffs,
	designed: [3]f64,
	state: []Svf_State,
	sample_rate: f64,
}
```

A state-variable filter node (see `svf_design`), stable under any
modulation: cutoff, Q and gain can be automated or ramped at audio rate.
Each output channel filters the matching input (silence for extra
outputs).

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `mode` |  |
| `cutoff` |  |
| `q` |  |
| `gain_db` |  |
| `coeffs` |  |
| `designed` | the cutoff, Q and gain `coeffs` are for |
| `state` | one per channel |
| `sample_rate` |  |

### Gain

```odin
Gain :: struct {
	gain: Smoothed_Value,
	ramp: Smoothed_Value,
	ramping: bool,
}
```

Gain stage with a sample-accurate, smoothed gain parameter (in dB).
Channel i of the output is channel i of the input (silence for extra outputs).
Its own smoothing moves in linear gain; automation ramps
(`core.Param_Ramp`) move linearly in dB, so an automated fade is exact at
any block size.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `gain` | linear gain: values and their smoothing |
| `ramp` | dB: an automation ramp, while `ramping` |
| `ramping` |  |

### Gate

```odin
Gate :: struct {
	threshold_db: f64,
	range_db: f64,
	ratio: f64,
	hysteresis_db: f64,
	attack_ms: f64,
	hold_ms: f64,
	release_ms: f64,
	open: bool,
	hold_left: int,
	detector: Level_Detector,
	gain: Gain_Smoother,
	sample_rate: f64,
	meter: u64,
}
```

A noise gate or downward expander node, stereo-linked. It opens when the
peak level rises above the threshold, and once it falls `hysteresis`
below it, closes after the hold time, turning down by up to `range` (by
`ratio` dB per dB under the threshold). Input channels beyond the
outputs are the sidechain, as for `Compressor`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `threshold_db` |  |
| `range_db` |  |
| `ratio` |  |
| `hysteresis_db` |  |
| `attack_ms` |  |
| `hold_ms` |  |
| `release_ms` |  |
| `open` |  |
| `hold_left` | frames |
| `detector` |  |
| `gain` |  |
| `sample_rate` |  |
| `meter` | atomic: f64 bits of the reduction in dB at the end of the last block |

### Limiter

```odin
Limiter :: struct {
	ceiling_db: f64,
	release_ms: f64,
	input: Smoothed_Value,
	lookahead: int,
	delay: []f32,
	need: []f64,
	window: Min_Window,
	sum: f64,
	box: []f64,
	gain: f64,
	release: f64,
	at: int,
	frames_since_sum: int,
	channels: int,
	lookahead_ms: f64,
	sample_rate: f64,
	meter: u64,
}
```

A lookahead peak limiter: no output sample is above the ceiling, ever.
It looks `lookahead_ms` ahead (reported as the node's latency, which the
graph compensates), finds the smallest gain any sample in that window
needs, and smooths it with a moving average of the same length, which
can never rise above what a sample needs while it plays; a slower
release then lets the gain recover. Stereo-linked.

The ceiling holds for samples, not for the waveform between them: after
a DAC or a sample-rate conversion, inter-sample peaks can be up to about
0.5 dB higher on dense material.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `ceiling_db` |  |
| `release_ms` |  |
| `input` | dB |
| `lookahead` | frames |
| `delay` | per channel ring of `lookahead`, flattened |
| `need` | ring of each frame's needed gain, `lookahead` long |
| `window` |  |
| `sum` | of the window minimums in the box, `lookahead` long |
| `box` | ring of the window minimums |
| `gain` | after the release |
| `release` | per-frame recovery coefficient |
| `at` | ring position |
| `frames_since_sum` |  |
| `channels` |  |
| `lookahead_ms` |  |
| `sample_rate` |  |
| `meter` | atomic: f64 bits of the gain reduction in dB at the end of the last block |

### Modulation

```odin
Modulation :: struct {...}
```

A chorus, flanger or phaser node (`chorus_create`, `flanger_create`,
`phaser_create`). Each channel has its own LFO phase, `spread` apart.
Fields are internal.

### One_Pole_Lowpass

```odin
One_Pole_Lowpass :: struct {
	cutoff: Smoothed_Value,
	g: f64,
	g_hz: f64,
	state: []f64,
	sample_rate: f64,
}
```

One-pole lowpass, topology-preserving transform (Zavalishin, "The Art of VA
Filter Design", ch. 3). Exactly -3.01 dB at cutoff thanks to prewarping.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `cutoff` | Hz |
| `g` | G = g / (1 + g), g = tan(pi fc / fs) |
| `g_hz` | the cutoff `g` is for |
| `state` | one per channel, allocated in prepare |
| `sample_rate` |  |

### Resampler_Quality

```odin
Resampler_Quality :: enum u8 {
	Low,
	Medium,
	High,
}
```

Interpolation quality: how much of the band is kept flat and how far
aliases are pushed down, at the cost of taps (multiply-adds) per output
sample and channel. Above speed 1 the filter widens by the speed, so the
taps grow with it. Medium suits clip playback; High suits offline work.

| Quality | Taps (speed ≤ 1) | Flat to (× Nyquist) | Aliases and images |
|---------|------------------|---------------------|--------------------|
| Low     | 32               | 0.75                | below −60 dB       |
| Medium  | 80               | 0.85                | below −90 dB       |
| High    | 160              | 0.90                | below −120 dB      |

### Resampler

```odin
Resampler :: struct {...}
```

Converts a stream between sample rates, or plays it faster or slower
(varispeed), with bandlimited interpolation: each output sample is a
Kaiser-windowed sinc evaluated at its exact position between input
samples (Julius O. Smith's method). The speed may change on every call.

Output frame k is the input at time `k × speed` (summed over calls), with
no added delay; the resampler only needs to see a little input ahead
(`resampler_input_needed` says how much). Planar f32. Set up with
`resampler_init`, free with `resampler_destroy`. Fields are internal.

### Reverb

```odin
Reverb :: struct {
	size: f64,
	decay_s: f64,
	hf_ratio: f64,
	predelay_ms: f64,
	diffusion: f64,
	modulation: f64,
	mix: Smoothed_Value,
	width: Smoothed_Value,
	lengths: [8]Smoothed_Value,
	gains: [8][2]f64,
	absorb: [8]f64,
	interp: [8]f64,
	primed: bool,
	lines: [8]Delay_Line,
	diffusers: [4]Delay_Line,
	diffuser_frames: [4]int,
	pre: Delay_Line,
	lfo_phase: [8]f64,
	sample_rate: f64,
}
```

An algorithmic reverb node: an 8-line feedback delay network (Jot and
Chaigne, "Digital Delay Networks for Designing Artificial Reverberators",
AES 1991). The lines feed back through a Hadamard matrix, which mixes
them losslessly, and each line's absorption filter sets the decay time
at low and at high frequencies exactly. Input is summed to mono,
delayed and diffused by allpass filters; output is stereo (every output
channel past the second is silent), the reverb mixed with the dry input.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `size` |  |
| `decay_s` |  |
| `hf_ratio` |  |
| `predelay_ms` |  |
| `diffusion` |  |
| `modulation` |  |
| `mix` |  |
| `width` | percent |
| `lengths` | frames, gliding when the size changes |
| `gains` | absorption filter b, a |
| `absorb` | filter states |
| `interp` | allpass interpolator states |
| `primed` | has rendered: before that, size changes jump instead of gliding |
| `lines` |  |
| `diffusers` |  |
| `diffuser_frames` |  |
| `pre` |  |
| `lfo_phase` |  |
| `sample_rate` |  |

### Smoothed_Value

```odin
Smoothed_Value :: struct {
	current: f64,
	target: f64,
	mode: core.Param_Smoothing,
	step: f64,
	remaining: int,
	ramp_len: int,
	coeff: f64,
	ramp_step: f64,
	ramp_left: int,
}
```

Per-sample parameter smoother. Nodes own one per smoothed parameter.
Advancing is per sample, so the result never depends on block boundaries.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `current` | value at the last `smoothed_next` |
| `target` | value being approached |
| `mode` |  |
| `step` | Linear |
| `remaining` |  |
| `ramp_len` |  |
| `coeff` | One-pole |
| `ramp_step` | A `smoothed_ramp` in progress (any mode) |
| `ramp_left` |  |

### Stft_Spectrum

```odin
Stft_Spectrum :: enum u8 {
	Packed,
	Half_Bin,
	Unpacked,
}
```

How an `Stft` lays out its spectrum.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Packed` | fft_size/2 bins; bin 0 holds DC (real) and Nyquist (imaginary) |
| `Half_Bin` | fft_size/2 bins at k + ½ (see `Real_Fft`); suits spectral processing |
| `Unpacked` | fft_size/2 + 1 bins, Nyquist in its own bin |

### Stft_Window

```odin
Stft_Window :: enum u8 {
	Keep,
	Acg,
	Kaiser,
}
```

The window shape `stft_set_interval` builds.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Keep` | leave the windows as they are |
| `Acg` | approximate confined Gaussian |
| `Kaiser` | Kaiser, with a bandwidth chosen for the interval |

### Stft_Normalisation

```odin
Stft_Normalisation :: enum u8 {
	Round_Trip,
	Synthesis,
	None,
}
```

What output is divided by, so that analysis then synthesis gives back the
input whatever the windows and block positions.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Round_Trip` | analysis × synthesis windows (the default) |
| `Synthesis` | the synthesis window only |
| `None` | only the FFT's gain |

### Stft

```odin
Stft :: struct {...}
```

A short-time Fourier transform for spectral processing: write input,
analyse a block into spectra, change the spectra, synthesise them back,
read output. It normalises itself: output is divided by the sum of the
window products of the blocks that went into it, so analysis then
synthesis at a steady hop (not only the default interval) reconstructs
the input exactly, `stft_latency` minus one hop later when output is read
straight after synthesising. (With uneven hops the gain varies, exactly
as in Signalsmith Linear.)

Analysis and synthesis can also run in steps (`stft_analyse_steps`), to
spread their cost. Planar f32; nothing allocates after `stft_init`.
Fields are internal.

### Stft_Input

```odin
Stft_Input :: struct {
	pos: int,
	buffer: []f32,
}
```

An STFT's input history, which can be saved and swapped (as Signalsmith
Stretch does to re-analyse). Make one with `stft_input_make`. Fields are
internal.

### Stft_Output

```odin
Stft_Output :: struct {...}
```

An STFT's pending output, which can be saved and swapped. Make one with
`stft_output_make`. Fields are internal.

### Stft_Settings

```odin
Stft_Settings :: struct {
	in_channels: int,
	out_channels: int,
	block: int,
	extra_history: int,
	interval: int,
	asymmetry: f64,
	fft_min_size: int,
	spectrum: Stft_Spectrum,
	split: bool,
}
```

Settings for `stft_init`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `in_channels` | channels analysed |
| `out_channels` | channels synthesised |
| `block` | block (window) length in samples |
| `extra_history` | input kept beyond one block, for analysing in the past |
| `interval` | default hop; 0 = block/4 |
| `asymmetry` | window warp, −1..1; 0 = symmetric |
| `fft_min_size` | 0 = block |
| `spectrum` |  |
| `split` | allow analysing and synthesising in more, smaller steps |

### Filter_Mode

```odin
Filter_Mode :: enum u8 {
	Lowpass,
	Highpass,
	Bandpass,
	Notch,
	Peak,
	Allpass,
	Bell,
	Low_Shelf,
	High_Shelf,
}
```

What a filter does. Cutoff is where a lowpass or highpass is −3 dB (at
Q = 0.707), the centre of a bandpass, notch, peak or bell, and the
midpoint (half the gain) of a shelf.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Lowpass` |  |
| `Highpass` |  |
| `Bandpass` | 0 dB at the cutoff |
| `Notch` |  |
| `Peak` | a resonance: lowpass minus highpass |
| `Allpass` | flat; phase only |
| `Bell` | boost or cut by `gain_db` around the cutoff |
| `Low_Shelf` | `gain_db` below the cutoff |
| `High_Shelf` | `gain_db` above the cutoff |

```odin
Svf_Coeffs :: struct {

	m1: f64,
	m2: f64,
}
```

Coefficients of a state-variable filter, from `svf_design`. Any number of
`Svf_State`s (one per channel) can share them.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `g` |  |
| `k` | prewarped cutoff, damping |
| `a1` |  |
| `a2` |  |
| `a3` |  |
| `m0` |  |
| `m1` |  |
| `m2` | the mode's mix of input, band and low outputs |

### Svf_State

```odin
Svf_State :: struct {
	ic1: f64,
	ic2: f64,
}
```

One channel's state of a state-variable filter.

## Procedures

### biquad_design

```odin
biquad_design :: proc "contextless"(mode: Filter_Mode, cutoff_hz: f64, q: f64, gain_db: f64, sample_rate: f64) -> Biquad_Coeffs
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Designs a biquad from Robert Bristow-Johnson's "Audio EQ Cookbook"
formulas: the same responses as `svf_design` (the bilinear transform with
the cutoff prewarped), so the two are interchangeable for fixed filters.
Prefer the SVF for anything modulated: a biquad's coefficients jumping
while it runs can click or, at high Q, blow up. Shelves use the
cookbook's slope S = 1 when `q` is 0.707 (the same curve the SVF gives).

### biquad_tick

```odin
biquad_tick :: proc "contextless"(c: ^Biquad_Coeffs, s: ^Biquad_State, x: f64) -> f64
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Filters one sample.

### biquad_process

```odin
biquad_process :: proc "contextless"(c: ^Biquad_Coeffs, s: ^Biquad_State, buf: []f32)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Filters `buf` in place with one channel's state.

### biquad_response

```odin
biquad_response :: proc "contextless"(c: ^Biquad_Coeffs, freq_hz: f64, sample_rate: f64) -> (gain: f64, phase: f64)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The response at `freq_hz`: gain (linear) and phase in radians.

### compressor_create

```odin
compressor_create :: proc(allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> core.Node
```

Control thread. Allocates a `Compressor` node at its defaults. Free it
with `core.node_destroy`.

### compressor_gain_reduction_db

```odin
compressor_gain_reduction_db :: proc "contextless"(c: ^Compressor) -> f64
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The compressor's gain reduction in dB at the end of its last block,
for a meter. Any thread.

### convolver_init

```odin
convolver_init :: proc(c: ^Convolver, ir: []f32, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (err: core.Error)
```

Control thread. Prepares a convolver for impulse response `ir` (any
length ≥ 1; copied). Free with `convolver_destroy`.

### convolver_destroy

```odin
convolver_destroy :: proc(c: ^Convolver, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator)
```

Control thread. Frees what `convolver_init` allocated.

### convolver_reset

```odin
convolver_reset :: proc "contextless"(c: ^Convolver)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Silences the convolver's memory of past input.

### convolver_process

```odin
convolver_process :: proc "contextless"(c: ^Convolver, input: []f32, output: []f32)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Convolves `input` into `output` (the same length; they may be the
same slice). Any length per call: the result never depends on how the
signal is split into calls.

### convolution_create

```odin
convolution_create :: proc(ir: [][]f32, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> core.Node
```

Control thread. A `Convolution` node with impulse response `ir` (planar,
copied). The FFTs of the response are made when the node is prepared.
Free it with `core.node_destroy`.

### delay_create

```odin
delay_create :: proc(allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> core.Node
```

Control thread. Allocates a `Delay` node at its defaults. Free it with
`core.node_destroy`.

### delay_line_init

```odin
delay_line_init :: proc(d: ^Delay_Line, max_delay: int, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. Allocates a delay line that can delay by up to
`max_delay` frames (plus room for interpolation). Free with
`delay_line_destroy`.

### delay_line_destroy

```odin
delay_line_destroy :: proc(d: ^Delay_Line, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator)
```

Control thread. Frees the delay line.

### delay_line_clear

```odin
delay_line_clear :: proc "contextless"(d: ^Delay_Line)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Silences the delay line.

### delay_line_write

```odin
delay_line_write :: proc "contextless"(d: ^Delay_Line, x: f32)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Adds the next frame.

### delay_line_read

```odin
delay_line_read :: proc "contextless"(d: ^Delay_Line, delay: f64, interp: Interpolation = Interpolation.Linear) -> f32
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The frame written `delay` frames before the last write (0 = the last
write). `delay` is clamped to what the line holds; Cubic reads at least 1
frame back.

### lfo_set_rate

```odin
lfo_set_rate :: proc "contextless"(l: ^Lfo, hz: f64, sample_rate: f64)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Sets the rate in Hz.

### lfo_shape_at

```odin
lfo_shape_at :: proc "contextless"(shape: Lfo_Shape, phase: f64) -> f64
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The shape's value at `phase` (0..1, wrapping). Random returns 0;
use `lfo_next` for it.

### lfo_next

```odin
lfo_next :: proc "contextless"(l: ^Lfo) -> f64
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The value now, then advances one frame.

### lfo_sync

```odin
lfo_sync :: proc "contextless"(l: ^Lfo, beat: f64, period_beats: f64)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Locks the LFO to the beat: one cycle per `period_beats`, at phase 0
on every multiple of it, from timeline position `beat`. Call it once
per block with the position at the block's start, and set the step from
the tempo (`lfo_set_rate(l, bpm / 60 / period_beats, sample_rate)`).

### compressor_curve

```odin
compressor_curve :: proc "contextless"(level_db: f64, threshold_db: f64, ratio: f64, knee_db: f64) -> f64
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The static curve of a downward compressor: the gain reduction in dB
(≥ 0) for a level of `level_db`, with a soft knee `knee_db` wide centred
on the threshold (Giannoulis, Massberg and Reiss, "Digital Dynamic Range
Compressor Design — A Tutorial and Analysis", JAES 2012, eq. 4).

### expander_curve

```odin
expander_curve :: proc "contextless"(level_db: f64, threshold_db: f64, ratio: f64, knee_db: f64, range_db: f64) -> f64
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The static curve of a downward expander (a gate at infinite ratio):
the gain reduction in dB (≥ 0, at most `range_db`) for a level of
`level_db`, with the same soft knee as `compressor_curve`.

### time_coeff

```odin
time_coeff :: proc "contextless"(time_ms: f64, sample_rate: f64) -> f64
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The per-sample coefficient of a one-pole smoother that covers
1 − 1/e (63%) of a step in `time_ms`.

### gain_smoother_next

```odin
gain_smoother_next :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Gain_Smoother, target_db: f64) -> f64
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Moves towards a gain reduction of `target_db`: attacking when it
must reduce more, releasing when less. Returns the new reduction in dB.

### level_detector_next

```odin
level_detector_next :: proc "contextless"(d: ^Level_Detector, frame: []f64) -> f64
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The detector's level in dB for one frame, from the samples of every
detected channel at that frame.

### eq_band_param

```odin
eq_band_param :: proc "contextless"(band: int, field: Eq_Band_Field) -> core.Param_Id
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The stable parameter id of band `band`'s (0-based) `field`:
100 + 10 × band + field.

### eq_create

```odin
eq_create :: proc(bands: int = 4, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> core.Node
```

Control thread. Allocates an `Eq` node of `bands` bands (1..EQ_MAX_BANDS),
all on and flat (0 dB) at first: a low shelf, bells spread over the
spectrum, and a high shelf. Free it with `core.node_destroy`.

### eq_response

```odin
eq_response :: proc "contextless"(q: ^Eq, freq_hz: f64) -> f64
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The EQ's combined gain (linear) at `freq_hz`, with its current
settings: for drawing its curve. Reads node state the audio thread
writes, so call it from the audio thread or accept a torn read.

### fft_fast_size_above

```odin
fft_fast_size_above :: proc "contextless"(size: int) -> int
```

The smallest size ≥ `size` that `Fft` handles quickly: a power of two
times 1, 3, 5, 6 or 8 (as Signalsmith Linear chooses, so ported code gets
the same sizes).

### fft_init

```odin
fft_init :: proc(f: ^Fft, size: int, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. Prepares an FFT of `size` (≥ 1, prime factors 2, 3, 5
only; `.Invalid_Argument` otherwise). Free with `fft_destroy`.

### fft_destroy

```odin
fft_destroy :: proc(f: ^Fft, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator)
```

Control thread. Frees what `fft_init` allocated.

### fft_steps

```odin
fft_steps :: proc "contextless"(f: ^Fft) -> int
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The number of steps a transform takes with `fft_forward_step` or
`fft_inverse_step`.

### fft_forward

```odin
fft_forward :: proc "contextless"(f: ^Fft, input: []complex64, output: []complex64)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Forward transform of `input` into `output` (both `size` long; they
may be the same slice).

### fft_inverse

```odin
fft_inverse :: proc "contextless"(f: ^Fft, input: []complex64, output: []complex64)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Inverse transform (unnormalised: scale by 1/size yourself).

### fft_forward_step

```odin
fft_forward_step :: proc "contextless"(f: ^Fft, step: int, input: []complex64, output: []complex64)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Step `step` (0 ..< fft_steps) of a forward transform. Run every step
in order, with the same slices, before using `output`.

### fft_inverse_step

```odin
fft_inverse_step :: proc "contextless"(f: ^Fft, step: int, input: []complex64, output: []complex64)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Step `step` of an inverse transform (see `fft_forward_step`).

### real_fft_fast_size_above

```odin
real_fft_fast_size_above :: proc "contextless"(size: int) -> int
```

The smallest even size ≥ `size` that `Real_Fft` handles quickly.

### real_fft_init

```odin
real_fft_init :: proc(r: ^Real_Fft, size: int, half_bin: bool = false, split: bool = false, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. Prepares a real FFT of `size` (even, size/2 with prime
factors 2, 3 and 5 only). Free with `real_fft_destroy`.

### real_fft_destroy

```odin
real_fft_destroy :: proc(r: ^Real_Fft, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator)
```

Control thread. Frees what `real_fft_init` allocated.

### real_fft_steps

```odin
real_fft_steps :: proc "contextless"(r: ^Real_Fft) -> int
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Steps per transform (forward or inverse).

### real_fft_forward

```odin
real_fft_forward :: proc "contextless"(r: ^Real_Fft, time: []f32, freq: []complex64)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Forward transform: `size` samples to `size`/2 bins.

### real_fft_inverse

```odin
real_fft_inverse :: proc "contextless"(r: ^Real_Fft, freq: []complex64, time: []f32)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Inverse transform: `size`/2 bins to `size` samples (unnormalised).

### real_fft_forward_step

```odin
real_fft_forward_step :: proc "contextless"(r: ^Real_Fft, step: int, time: []f32, freq: []complex64)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Step `step` of a forward transform (0 ..< real_fft_steps). Run every
step in order, with the same slices.

### real_fft_inverse_step

```odin
real_fft_inverse_step :: proc "contextless"(r: ^Real_Fft, step: int, freq: []complex64, time: []f32)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Step `step` of an inverse transform (see `real_fft_forward_step`).

### filter_create

```odin
filter_create :: proc(mode: Filter_Mode = Filter_Mode.Lowpass, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> core.Node
```

Control thread. Allocates a `Filter` node starting in `mode`. Free it with
`core.node_destroy`.

### gain_create

```odin
gain_create :: proc(allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> core.Node
```

Control thread. Allocates a `Gain` node with `allocator`. Free it with
`core.node_destroy`.

### db_to_gain

```odin
db_to_gain :: proc "contextless"(db: f64) -> f64
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Converts decibels to linear gain. Returns exactly 0 at -96 dB and below.

### gate_create

```odin
gate_create :: proc(allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> core.Node
```

Control thread. Allocates a `Gate` node at its defaults. Free it with
`core.node_destroy`.

### gate_reduction_db

```odin
gate_reduction_db :: proc "contextless"(g: ^Gate) -> f64
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The gate's gain reduction in dB at the end of its last block. Any thread.

### limiter_create

```odin
limiter_create :: proc(lookahead_ms: f64 = 5.0, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> core.Node
```

Control thread. Allocates a `Limiter` node looking `lookahead_ms` ahead
(0.1..50; its latency, fixed for the node's life). Free it with
`core.node_destroy`.

### limiter_gain_reduction_db

```odin
limiter_gain_reduction_db :: proc "contextless"(l: ^Limiter) -> f64
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The limiter's gain reduction in dB at the end of its last block. Any thread.

### chorus_create

```odin
chorus_create :: proc(allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> core.Node
```

Control thread. A chorus node: up to 4 voices per channel, each a copy
delayed by `delay` ± `depth` ms on its own LFO phase, mixed with the dry
signal. Free it with `core.node_destroy`.

### flanger_create

```odin
flanger_create :: proc(allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> core.Node
```

Control thread. A flanger node: a short delay swept by an LFO, mixed with
the dry signal into moving comb-filter notches; feedback sharpens them.

### phaser_create

```odin
phaser_create :: proc(allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> core.Node
```

Control thread. A phaser node: a chain of first-order allpass filters
(TPT, so sweeping is smooth) whose frequency an LFO sweeps on a log
scale between `min` and `max`, mixed with the dry signal. Every two
stages make one notch; at 50% mix the notches are complete.

### one_pole_create

```odin
one_pole_create :: proc(allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> core.Node
```

Control thread. Allocates a `One_Pole_Lowpass` node with `allocator`. Free it
with `core.node_destroy`. Each output channel filters the matching input
channel (silence for extra outputs).

### resampler_init

```odin
resampler_init :: proc(r: ^Resampler, channels: int, quality: Resampler_Quality = Resampler_Quality.High, max_speed: f64 = 4, max_input: int = 4096, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. Prepares `r` for `channels` channels, speeds up to
`max_speed` (input frames per output frame; ≥ 1) and input given in pieces
of up to `max_input` frames. Free with `resampler_destroy`.

### resampler_destroy

```odin
resampler_destroy :: proc(r: ^Resampler, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator)
```

Control thread. Frees what `resampler_init` allocated.

### resampler_reset

```odin
resampler_reset :: proc "contextless"(r: ^Resampler)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Forgets all input: the next output frame is the next input frame,
preceded by silence.

### resampler_input_needed

```odin
resampler_input_needed :: proc "contextless"(r: ^Resampler, out_frames: int, speed: f64) -> int
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Input frames to add before `out_frames` more output frames can be
produced at `speed` (0 if enough is buffered). For pull-style playback:
read this many frames, then call `resampler_process` once.

### resampler_process

```odin
resampler_process :: proc "contextless"(r: ^Resampler, input: [][]f32, output: [][]f32, speed: f64) -> (consumed: int, produced: int)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Resamples at `speed` input frames per output frame (> 0, at most
`max_speed`): takes frames from `input` (one slice per channel, all the
same length) and writes frames to `output` (likewise) until the input is
used up or the output is full. Returns how many frames were consumed and
produced. Never allocates.

### reverb_create

```odin
reverb_create :: proc(allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> core.Node
```

Control thread. Allocates a `Reverb` node at its defaults. Free it with
`core.node_destroy`.

### smoothed_init

```odin
smoothed_init :: proc(s: ^Smoothed_Value, value: f64, mode: core.Param_Smoothing, time_ms: f64, sample_rate: f64)
```

Control thread (prepare). `time_ms` is the linear ramp length or the one-pole time constant.

### smoothed_init_from_param

```odin
smoothed_init_from_param :: proc(s: ^Smoothed_Value, p: core.Param_Info, sample_rate: f64)
```

Control thread (prepare). `smoothed_init` with the parameter's default value,
smoothing mode and smoothing time.

### smoothed_set_target

```odin
smoothed_set_target :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Smoothed_Value, target: f64)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Starts moving toward `target`. With `.None` smoothing the value jumps;
with `.Linear` a new ramp of the full length starts from the current value.

### smoothed_ramp

```odin
smoothed_ramp :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Smoothed_Value, target: f64, frames: int)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Moves in a straight line from the current value to `target`,
whatever the smoothing mode, as `core.Param_Ramp` asks: the next
`smoothed_next` still returns the current value, and the one `frames`
calls later returns `target` (for 0, the next one already does).

### smoothed_apply

```odin
smoothed_apply :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Smoothed_Value, value: f64, ramp_frames: int)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Applies a parameter change read by `core.param_event`: a ramp when
`ramp_frames` ≥ 0, otherwise the parameter's own smoothing.

### smoothed_reset

```odin
smoothed_reset :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Smoothed_Value, value: f64)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Jump to `value` with no ramp.

### smoothed_is_smoothing

```odin
smoothed_is_smoothing :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Smoothed_Value) -> bool
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Reports whether the value has not yet reached its target.

### smoothed_next

```odin
smoothed_next :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Smoothed_Value) -> f64
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Advance one sample and return the new value.

### stft_init

```odin
stft_init :: proc(s: ^Stft, settings: Stft_Settings, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. Allocates and configures an STFT (with an ACG window at
the default interval, and round-trip normalisation), then resets it. Free
with `stft_destroy`.

### stft_destroy

```odin
stft_destroy :: proc(s: ^Stft, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator)
```

Control thread. Frees what `stft_init` allocated.

### stft_input_make

```odin
stft_input_make :: proc(s: ^Stft, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> Stft_Input
```

Control thread. A spare input state the same size as `s`'s, for saving
and swapping (see `stft_input_copy`, `stft_swap_input`).

### stft_output_make

```odin
stft_output_make :: proc(s: ^Stft, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> Stft_Output
```

Control thread. A spare output state the same size as `s`'s.

### stft_input_free

```odin
stft_input_free :: proc(state: ^Stft_Input, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator)
```

Control thread. Frees a spare state from `stft_input_make`.

### stft_output_free

```odin
stft_output_free :: proc(state: ^Stft_Output, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator)
```

Control thread. Frees a spare state from `stft_output_make`.

```odin
stft_input_copy :: proc "contextless"(dst: ^Stft_Input, src: ^Stft_Input)
```

```odin
stft_output_copy :: proc "contextless"(dst: ^Stft_Output, src: ^Stft_Output)
```

```odin
stft_swap_output :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, other: ^Stft_Output)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Exchanges the STFT's output state with `other`.



### stft_analysis_latency

```odin
stft_analysis_latency :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft) -> int
```

### stft_synthesis_latency

```odin
stft_synthesis_latency :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft) -> int
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Samples from the centre of the synthesis window to the output read next.

### stft_latency

```odin
stft_latency :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft) -> int
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Total latency through analysis and synthesis.

### stft_samples_since_analysis

```odin
stft_samples_since_analysis :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft) -> int
```

### stft_samples_since_synthesis

```odin
stft_samples_since_synthesis :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft) -> int
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Output moved since the last synthesis.

```odin
stft_bin_to_freq :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, bin: f32) -> f32
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). A bin's frequency as a fraction of the sample rate.

### stft_freq_to_bin

```odin
stft_freq_to_bin :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, freq: f32) -> f32
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The (fractional) bin of a frequency given as a fraction of the sample rate.

### stft_spectrum

```odin

```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Channel `channel`'s spectrum: `stft_bands` bins, read and written in
place between analysis and synthesis.

### stft_analysis_window

```odin
stft_analysis_window :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft) -> []f32
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The analysis window (`stft_block` samples), editable.

### stft_synthesis_window

```odin
stft_synthesis_window :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft) -> []f32
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The synthesis window, editable.

### stft_set_analysis_offset

```odin
stft_set_analysis_offset :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, offset: int)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Sets the index of the analysis window's centre.

### stft_set_synthesis_offset

```odin
stft_set_synthesis_offset :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, offset: int)
```

### stft_set_normalisation

```odin
stft_set_normalisation :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, mode: Stft_Normalisation)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Sets how output is normalised.

### stft_reset

```odin
stft_reset :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, product_weight: f32 = 1)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Clears all input and output. `product_weight` scales the initial
window products (the output's starting normalisation).

### stft_set_interval

```odin
stft_set_interval :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, interval: int, shape: Stft_Window = Stft_Window.Keep, asymmetry: f64 = 0)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Sets the default hop, and (unless `.Keep`) rebuilds both windows for
it. Windows are made in f64. With no asymmetry, the windows are scaled for
perfect reconstruction at this hop.

### stft_write_input

```odin
stft_write_input :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, channel: int, offset: int, samples: []f32)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Writes `samples` into channel `channel`'s input, `offset` samples
after the current input position (which doesn't move).

### stft_move_input

```odin
stft_move_input :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, samples: int, clear: bool = false)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Moves the input position on by `samples` (optionally clearing what
it moves over first).

### stft_read_output

```odin
stft_read_output :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, channel: int, offset: int, out: []f32)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Reads `len(out)` samples of channel `channel`'s output, starting
`offset` samples ahead, normalised.

### stft_add_output

```odin
stft_add_output :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, channel: int, offset: int, samples: []f32)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Adds `samples` (already normalised) into channel `channel`'s output,
`offset` samples ahead (at most one block).

### stft_replace_output

```odin
stft_replace_output :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, channel: int, offset: int, samples: []f32)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Like `stft_add_output`, but replacing what was there.

### stft_move_output

```odin
stft_move_output :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, samples: int)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Moves the output position on by `samples`, clearing what it passes.

### stft_finish_output

```odin
stft_finish_output :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, strength: f32 = 1, offset: int = 0)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). When no more synthesis is coming, lets the output taper to zero with
the windows rather than being scaled up as if blocks were just far apart.
Applies from `offset` samples ahead; `strength` 0..1.

### stft_analyse

```odin
stft_analyse :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, samples_in_past: int = 0)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Analyses the latest block of input (or one ending `samples_in_past`
samples ago) into every channel's spectrum.

### stft_analyse_steps

```odin
stft_analyse_steps :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft) -> int
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Steps an analysis takes (one per channel, or more with `split`).

### stft_analyse_step

```odin
stft_analyse_step :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, step: int, samples_in_past: int = 0)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Step `step` of an analysis; run all of them in order.

### stft_synthesise

```odin
stft_synthesise :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Synthesises every channel's spectrum and adds the result to the
output at the current position.

### stft_synthesise_steps

```odin
stft_synthesise_steps :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft) -> int
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Steps a synthesis takes.

### stft_synthesise_step

```odin
stft_synthesise_step :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, step: int)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Step `step` of a synthesis; run all of them in order.

### svf_design

```odin
svf_design :: proc "contextless"(mode: Filter_Mode, cutoff_hz: f64, q: f64, gain_db: f64, sample_rate: f64) -> (c: Svf_Coeffs)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Designs a state-variable filter: Andrew Simper's linear trapezoidal
SVF ("Solving the continuous SVF equations using trapezoidal integration
and equivalent currents", Cytomic, 2013). Its response is the analog
prototype's, bilinear-transformed with the cutoff prewarped, and it stays
stable and smooth when its coefficients change every sample, so it suits
modulated filters. `q` > 0 (0.707 is flat); `gain_db` is for Bell and the
shelves. The cutoff is kept below 0.49 × `sample_rate`.

### svf_tick

```odin
svf_tick :: proc "contextless"(c: ^Svf_Coeffs, s: ^Svf_State, x: f64) -> f64
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Filters one sample.

### svf_process

```odin
svf_process :: proc "contextless"(c: ^Svf_Coeffs, s: ^Svf_State, buf: []f32)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Filters `buf` in place with one channel's state.

### svf_response

```odin
svf_response :: proc "contextless"(c: ^Svf_Coeffs, freq_hz: f64, sample_rate: f64) -> (gain: f64, phase: f64)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The filter's exact response at `freq_hz`: gain (linear) and phase in
radians. For drawing EQ curves.
